questions.question: The rate of a reaction doubles for each 10 K rise in temperature. By what factor does the rate increase when the temperature is raised from 298 K to 358 K? A 6, B 12, C 36, D 64.
steps: Temperature rise = 358 K - 298 K = 60 K
Number of 10 K steps = 60 / 10 = 6
Each 10 K step doubles the rate, so the factor = 2^6
2^6 = 64, so the answer is D

questions.question: Write the overall equation for Process A (ethene + chlorine, then cracking of 1,2-dichloroethane to chloroethene) and use it to calculate the percentage atom economy by mass for chloroethene.
questions.answer: C2H4 + Cl2 -> C2H3Cl + HCl; atom economy = 62.5 / 99.0 x 100 = 63.1% (about 63%)
steps: Stage 1: C2H4 + Cl2 -> C2H4Cl2 (addition)
Stage 2: C2H4Cl2 -> C2H3Cl + HCl (thermal cracking, elimination of HCl)
Overall: C2H4 + Cl2 -> C2H3Cl + HCl; HCl is a by-product
Mr of desired product C2H3Cl = 2(12.0) + 3(1.0) + 35.5 = 62.5
Total Mr of reactants = 28.0 + 71.0 = 99.0

questions.question: Compare Process A with Process B (ethyne + hydrogen chloride, using toxic mercury(II) chloride catalyst that vaporises at the reaction temperature) in terms of atom economy and environmental impact. No calculation is needed.
questions.answer: Process A has the lower atom economy (about 63%, HCl is wasted) but a lower environmental impact; Process B has 100% atom economy but uses toxic, vaporising HgCl2 catalyst
steps: Process B is an addition reaction (HCCH + HCl -> CH2=CHCl), so all atoms end up in the product
Atom economy of Process B is 100%, higher than Process A (about 63%)
Process A produces HCl as a waste by-product, lowering its atom economy
Process B uses mercury(II) chloride, which is highly toxic and vaporises, so it has the greater environmental impact

questions.question: Explain the effects on the rate of increasing the temperature and of using a catalyst in a gas reaction, referring to a labelled Maxwell-Boltzmann distribution diagram.
questions.answer: Higher temperature: more particles have E >= Ea, more frequent and more energetic collisions. Catalyst: lower Ea, more particles have E >= Ea, so rate increases; the distribution itself is unchanged.
steps: Draw the curve with energy on the x-axis and number of molecules on the y-axis, with Ea marked
Higher temperature: the curve flattens and shifts right, so a larger fraction of molecules has E >= Ea
Higher temperature also gives more frequent and more energetic collisions, so more successful collisions per second
A catalyst provides an alternative route with a lower activation energy, shown by Ea moving left
More molecules now have E >= Ea, the area beyond Ea increases, so more successful collisions occur
The catalyst is unchanged at the end and the total number of molecules (area under curve) is the same, so the rate increases

questions.question: Sodium thiosulfate solution reacts with hydrochloric acid to produce solid sulfur. Which change would increase the time taken for sulfur to appear? A increase HCl concentration, B decrease thiosulfate concentration, C increase temperature, D add a catalyst.
questions.answer: B (decrease the concentration of sodium thiosulfate)
steps: Time for sulfur to appear is inversely proportional to the rate
Lower concentration of a reactant reduces collision frequency, so rate falls
Increasing HCl concentration, increasing temperature and adding a catalyst all increase the rate and shorten the time
So decreasing the thiosulfate concentration lengthens the time: answer B

questions.question: 0.100 mol of hydrochloric acid is added to 8.43 g of magnesium carbonate (Mr = 84.3). What is the total volume of carbon dioxide at r.t.p. (molar volume 24.0 dm3 per mol)? A 2.40 dm3, B 1.20 dm3, C 2400 dm3, D 1200 dm3.
steps: Moles of MgCO3 = 8.43 / 84.3 = 0.100 mol
Equation: MgCO3 + 2HCl -> MgCl2 + H2O + CO2
0.100 mol HCl needs only 0.050 mol MgCO3, so HCl is the limiting reagent
Moles of CO2 = 0.100 / 2 = 0.050 mol
Volume = 0.050 x 24.0 = 1.20 dm3, answer B

questions.question: Explain the type of reaction in Stage 1 of the Liebig Process, 6Ca(OH)2 + 6Cl2 -> Ca(ClO3)2 + 5CaCl2 + 6H2O, using oxidation numbers.
questions.answer: Disproportionation: chlorine (0) is oxidised to +5 in ClO3- and reduced to -1 in Cl- of CaCl2
steps: Oxidation number of Cl in Cl2 is 0
Cl in Ca(ClO3)2 (ClO3-) has oxidation number +5, so Cl is oxidised (loses 5 electrons per Cl)
Cl in CaCl2 has oxidation number -1, so Cl is reduced (gains 1 electron per Cl)
Ca, H and O keep the same oxidation numbers in every species
The same element is both oxidised and reduced, so this is a disproportionation (redox) reaction

Add aqueous silver nitrate solution
Chloride ions form a white precipitate of silver chloride, AgCl
Bromide ions would form a cream precipitate of silver bromide, AgBr
A white precipitate confirms chloride impurity (optionally, it dissolves in dilute ammonia while cream AgBr does not)

questions.question: Explain why calcium carbonate decomposes at a higher temperature than magnesium carbonate, in terms of the charge and size of the cations.
questions.answer: Ca2+ is larger than Mg2+ with the same charge, so it has lower charge density and polarises the carbonate ion less, so the carbonate is more stable
steps: Ca2+ and Mg2+ both have a 2+ charge
Ca2+ has a larger ionic radius than Mg2+, so its charge density is lower
A low charge density cation distorts (polarises) the carbonate ion less
Less distortion of the carbonate ion means the C-O bonds are less weakened, so more heat is needed to decompose it

questions.question: A gas syringe measures a maximum of 100 cm3 of CO2. Calculate the maximum volume of 0.500 mol dm-3 HCl that can be added to excess CaCO3 at r.t.p. without exceeding this volume. Molar volume = 24 000 cm3 mol-1.
steps: Moles of CO2 max = 100 / 24 000 = 4.17 x 10^-3 mol
CaCO3 + 2HCl -> CaCl2 + CO2 + H2O, so moles of HCl = 2 x 4.17 x 10^-3 = 8.33 x 10^-3 mol
Volume = moles / concentration = 8.33 x 10^-3 / 0.500 = 1.67 x 10^-2 dm3
Volume = 16.7 cm3

questions.question: A bottle of hydrogen peroxide is labelled 10 volume: 1 cm3 gives 10 cm3 of O2 at r.t.p. What is its concentration in mol dm-3? Molar volume = 24 000 cm3 mol-1. A 0.100, B 0.208, C 0.417, D 0.833.

From 2H2O2 -> 2H2O + O2, moles H2O2 = 2 x 4.17 x 10^-4 = 8.33 x 10^-4 mol
This amount is in 1 cm3 = 0.001 dm3
Concentration = 8.33 x 10^-4 / 0.001 = 0.833 mol dm-3, answer D

questions.question: A Maxwell-Boltzmann curve for particles in a reaction mixture is shown. Which statement is correct? A position X is the mean energy, B Ea is the mean energy of particles that react, C the area under the curve to the right of Ea gives the number of particles with enough energy to react, D a catalyst moves Ea to the right.
questions.answer: C
steps: The area under the curve to the right of Ea is the fraction of particles with energy >= Ea
These particles have enough energy to react
Ea is not the mean energy, so A and B are wrong
A catalyst lowers Ea (moves it left), so D is wrong

questions.question: What happens to the Maxwell-Boltzmann distribution when the temperature of the gas is decreased?
questions.answer: The peak moves to lower energy (left) and becomes higher and narrower; the total area stays the same
steps: Lower temperature means the average kinetic energy of molecules falls
The peak shifts to lower energy (left)
The curve becomes taller and narrower at the peak
The total area under the curve is unchanged because the number of molecules is the same, and fewer molecules now have E >= Ea

questions.question: For 2SO2(g) + O2(g) <=> 2SO3(g), dH = -192 kJ mol-1, what is the effect of a decrease in temperature? A rate increases and yield decreases, B rate increases and yield increases, C rate decreases and yield decreases, D rate decreases and yield increases.
questions.answer: D (rate decreases and yield increases)
steps: The forward reaction is exothermic (dH negative)
Lowering temperature shifts equilibrium to the exothermic side, so yield of SO3 increases
Lower temperature means lower average kinetic energy and fewer collisions with E >= Ea, so rate decreases
The answer is D

questions.question: For 2SO2(g) + O2(g) <=> 2SO3(g), what is the effect of an increase in pressure? A rate increases and yield decreases, B rate increases and yield increases, C rate decreases and yield decreases, D rate decreases and yield increases.
questions.answer: B (rate increases and yield increases)
steps: Pressure increases the concentration of gases, so rate increases
There are 3 mol of gas on the left and 2 mol on the right
Increasing pressure shifts equilibrium to the side with fewer gas moles, which is the right
Yield of SO3 increases, so the answer is B

questions.question: 1.0 cm3 of 0.20 mol dm-3 K2CrO4 and 5.0 cm3 of 1.0 mol dm-3 H2SO4 form an equilibrium. What is the effect on colour of adding 5.0 cm3 of 1.0 mol dm-3 NaOH? A no change, B colourless, C more yellow, D more orange.

steps: Equilibrium: 2CrO4^2- (yellow) + 2H+ <=> Cr2O7^2- (orange) + H2O
NaOH reacts with H+ ions, removing them from the mixture
Lower H+ concentration shifts the equilibrium to the left (Le Chatelier)
More yellow chromate(VI) ions form, so the mixture becomes more yellow

questions.question: The activation energy Ea of an uncatalysed reaction is shown on a Maxwell-Boltzmann curve with shaded areas A and B on either side of Ea. How do the two shaded areas change when a catalyst is added?
